observation: During the prompt workflow sync, agent-loop required a separately pinned agent-skills commit solely to provide skills/operational-prompting/operating-prompts.json to agent-recall-compiler. The same Recall-specific catalog and direct review instructions lived in agent-skills while Recall code, CLI behavior, manifest handling, and releases evolved independently. This created a manual cross-repository synchronization obligation and made green Loop gates depend on an unrelated skill-repository SHA for Recall behavior.

evidence.summary: agent-loop prompt-primitives and execution-contract workflows pinned agent-skills commit 2d43611e854f1621e62014a3f3b312ad2dc572b7 specifically to load skills/operational-prompting/operating-prompts.json while Recall was separately versioned at 0.11.4.
A Recall-owned copy of the catalog compiled adversarial-review through the real CLI and preserved the falsification-safe contract in package CI.

hypothesis: When a coding skill's correctness depends on a tool's CLI, schema, file layout, generated artifacts, or runtime behavior but its canonical instructions live elsewhere, code and instructions acquire independent release cadences and drift unless every consumer manually synchronizes both repositories.
validated_conclusion: Keep tool-coupled skills and machine-readable instruction assets in the repository that owns the tool. Ship and test them with the implementation. Generic skill collections may contain tool-neutral principles and may reference or install tool-owned skills, but must not keep a second canonical copy of tool commands, schemas, output contracts, or recipe resources.
